mechanism_narrative: A high level of GDPC1 indicates strong economic demand, which drives corporate earnings and thus increases S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 is high, but S&P 500 returns are not positive over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in UNRATE above 4.5% signals labor market tightening, leading to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises above 4.5%, but S&P 500 returns are not negative over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When both UNRATE is above 4.5% and FEDFUNDS is above 1.5%, the combined effect of labor market tightening and high interest rates leads to decreased S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Both conditions are met, but S&P 500 returns are not negative over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, increased housing starts (HOUST) signal strong demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: HOUST increases in late-cycle, but S&P 500 returns are not positive over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strong supply chains, leading to increased S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO is high, but S&P 500 returns are not positive over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 2%, higher interest rates reduce corporate borrowing, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS exceeds 2%, but S&P 500 returns are not negative over 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: When both PAYEMS and RSAFS are high, strong labor and retail sales indicate high demand, leading to increased S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Both proxies are high, but S&P 500 returns are not positive over 60 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime, rising FEDFUNDS leads to decreased S&P 500 returns over 20 days as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS rises, but S&P 500 returns are not negative over 20 days.
